close_reason: Landed in commit 5caf280. Per parent sgrr.17 ratification of option (c) doc-only hardening, this bead resolves identically: PartialDate.month and PartialDate.day rustdoc now explicitly says the type does not range-check, callers MUST verify 1..=12 / 1..=31 before treating as RFC 9553 §2.8.1-conformant. README Gotchas list gains a corresponding bullet cross-referencing bd:JMAP-sgrr.14 and bd:JMAP-sgrr.15 so the pattern of unbounded-numeric findings is visible.
description:
lib.rs:888-915 defines PartialDate.month at line 899 and PartialDate.day at
line 903 as Option<u32>. RFC 9553 §2.8.1 specifies month is 1..=12 and day is
1..=31 (with month-specific cap of 28/29/30/31). The crate's doc comment
mirrors the spec: 'Calendar month, 1..=12' / 'Calendar day of month, 1..=31'.

There is no validation. A caller can construct PartialDate { month: Some(13),
day: Some(32), year: Some(2024), ... } and it round-trips through serde. A
consumer reading the PartialDate has to range-check both fields themselves —
no helper, no Result-returning constructor, no validate method.

Cousin of JMAP-sgrr.5 (which is about UnsignedInt 2^32 vs 2^53) and JMAP-sgrr.15
(NonZeroU32 for list_as). The pattern recurs.

Two fixes:

(a) Newtypes: Month(NonZeroU8) capped at 12, Day(NonZeroU8) capped at 31. Both
    have validating constructors that return Result.
(b) Validate on the type via a deserialize_with helper, rejecting out-of-range
    on the deserialize path. Construction in Rust remains unchecked.

(a) catches the bug at compile time for Rust callers. (b) catches it only at
deserialize time. (a) is breaking to apply later; (b) is not.

This is a paper cut individually. Across PartialDate + the list_as / pref
fields in this crate, it adds up to a pattern of 'spec values have bounds the
type does not capture'. Worth deciding once.
title: PartialDate.month and PartialDate.day have no validation — month=13 and day=32 deserialize successfully
